title: Laurindo Almeida, Hav-a-Havana and other Kenton entries
summary: A samba with Laurindo Almeida, Birdland broadcasts, and why he titled a chart Hav-a-Havana.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: After you leave Kenton, what happens? By the way, when I‟m looking down here, there are no entries for Zoot Sims in here. Did he go by Jack Sims? Did he have any aliases? He‟s not credited on any of these. That may be yet another problem with this discography.
It would be in ‟53, probably summer of ‟53 he would have been there.

Okay. Let‟s scroll down and see if he‟s added. Oh, here‟s a very interesting one, when Laurindo Almeida was in the group, or at least recorded. This is showing in January of ‟53 he‟s recording with the Kenton orchestra.
Yeah. We did a South American tune, I think. A samba, maybe.
Which predates the bossa craze that came in towards the end of that decade. What was it like? Did you know Laurindo?
I met him. That‟s about all, because he didn‟t travel with the band at all.

Here‟s some more radio broadcasts, all the way down through January. Then here‟s a recording, 23 Degrees North, 82 Degrees West. You‟re credited here as an arranger as well. But it‟s still the same tunes. It‟s got Works credited to you here. I‟m going to continue to scroll down. April. This is in Chicago. All About Ronnie. You‟re not the arranger on that one. Let me see if I can find another. How about Hav-a-Havana and Frank Speaking. These are broadcasts from Birdland in April of ‟53. These give credit to you for these arrangements.
Excuse me. You‟re right. I‟m sorry. It‟s Hav-a-Havana.
Was that in reference to the cigar?
Yeah. I wanted to think of something in Cuba. I remembered having seen those billboards and ads. It‟s the Cuba connection.
